Pensieve's core idea — treat conversation state as a cross-request cache owner so repeated history is not reprocessed — maps directly onto the encoder cache: in agentic loops, the same images/audio recur turn after turn, but today encoder_cache_size is provisioned only for a single largest item, forcing re-encoding under pressure. The finding contributes the concrete, transferable shift from 'size for one item' to 'size for retained per-session items', addressing the gap that the current static max(...) policy does not adapt to expected retained media across turns. This is the budget-side complement to runtime retention and is the smallest change to compute_mm_encoder_budget that lets the existing EncoderCacheManager hit-path actually serve repeated media without thrashing.

agent_proposals.title: Denominate encoder_compute_budget in modality-weighted compute-equivalent tokens, not raw tokens
agent_proposals.detailed_description:
In compute_mm_encoder_budget (vllm/v1/core/encoder_cache_manager.py:269-316), change the unit in which encoder_compute_budget is expressed from raw multimodal-token counts to modality-cost-weighted equivalent tokens, while leaving encoder_cache_size in raw token units (since cache footprint is genuinely per-token).

Concretely:

1) Introduce a per-modality compute-cost coefficient `c_mod` representing the encoder forward FLOPs per output token of modality `mod` divided by a reference modality's FLOPs per token (image-patch encoder = 1.0 by default). Source the coefficients in this order: (a) an explicit SchedulerConfig.mm_encoder_cost_coeffs dict, (b) a per-model registry keyed on the multimodal config (vision tower depth, video temporal stride, audio mel-spectrogram window) computed once at startup, (c) fallback 1.0 to preserve current behavior.

2) Replace the line that sets `max_tokens_per_mm_item = max(mm_max_toks_per_item.values())` for the *compute* path with a weighted form: `max_compute_equiv_per_item = max(c_mod * mm_max_toks_per_item[mod] for mod in mm_max_toks_per_item)`. Use this quantity for the `encoder_compute_budget = max(configured_compute, max_compute_equiv_per_item)` assignment and for the `disable_chunked_mm_input` validation, so a video item that is cheap-per-token but token-numerous does not reserve as much per-step encoder compute as a smaller-but-FLOP-heavier image item, and vice versa.

3) Keep `encoder_cache_size = max(configured_cache, max(mm_max_toks_per_item.values()))` in raw token units. The cache stores encoder outputs whose memory footprint is linear in tokens regardless of producing modality, so weighting cache sizing would be incorrect.

4) Plumb the coefficients to Scheduler._try_schedule_encoder_inputs so its admission test charges encoder work in the same compute-equivalent unit; an explicit `encoder_tokens_to_compute_equiv(num_tokens, modality)` helper on EncoderCacheManager keeps the conversion in one place. Defaults of 1.0 reproduce today's numbers exactly, so existing tests in tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py and tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py pass unchanged; new tests should verify that with non-unit coefficients the per-step admitted token count tracks the FLOP budget (e.g., a 0.3x-cost audio modality admits ~3.3x more audio tokens per step than the image baseline).

This is a unit-system change to the existing static max(...) policy, not a new dynamic mechanism, so it composes cleanly with any of the listed concurrency/reuse-based cache-sizing proposals: those would still operate on raw token counts for cache_size, while encoder_compute_budget would now be expressed in compute-equivalent units that reflect actual stall risk.
agent_proposals.novelty_rationale: Every listed deep_research_proposal arithmetic-operates on raw multimodal token counts: find-0001 separates compute vs cache and offers per-modality budgets but still in token units; find-0007 caps compute at a fraction of max_num_batched_tokens (token-denominated); find-0009/0011/0013/0017 all multiply max_tokens_per_mm_item by concurrency or reuse factors. None addresses that a token of one modality costs a different number of encoder FLOPs than a token of another modality - so a token-denominated compute budget systematically over-admits cheap-per-token modalities (e.g., audio mel patches) and under-admits expensive ones (e.g., dense video temporal attention), which directly affects TPOT in mixed-modality agentic workloads. The proposal switches the *unit* of the compute budget from raw tokens to modality-weighted compute-equivalent tokens; this is orthogonal to the existing proposals' headroom/concurrency/reuse multipliers and complements them rather than restating them. It also explicitly preserves raw-token sizing for cache_size, separating a unit concern that all prior findings conflate.

agent_proposals.title: Validate disabled MM chunking against placeholder span, not encoder-embed count
agent_proposals.detailed_description: In `vllm/v1/core/encoder_cache_manager.py:269-316`, separate the unit used for the `disable_chunked_mm_input` validation from the unit used for encoder compute/cache capacity. Today `mm_max_toks_per_item` is derived from `PlaceholderRange.get_num_embeds()`, but `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` decides whether an MM item is chunked using `mm_position.length`. For masked or embedding-sparse placeholders, `length` can be much larger than `get_num_embeds()`, so startup can accept `disable_chunked_mm_input=True` even when the scheduler cannot fit the full placeholder span in one `max_num_batched_tokens` step. Add a companion per-modality max placeholder-span value from the multimodal dummy placeholders, pass it into `compute_mm_encoder_budget`, and use `max_placeholder_tokens_per_mm_item > scheduler_config.max_num_batched_tokens` for the disabled-chunking `ValueError`. Keep `encoder_compute_budget` and `encoder_cache_size` based on encoder-embed counts, since those are the resources consumed by encoder execution and cache storage. Add tests covering a placeholder with `length=128`, `get_num_embeds()=8`, `max_num_batched_tokens=64`, and `disable_chunked_mm_input=True`, which should now fail fast; the same case with chunking enabled should preserve current budget values.
agent_proposals.novelty_rationale: The deep research proposals focus on concurrency, reuse, SLO-aware cache sizing, compute/cache decoupling, and batched-token headroom. Agent A focuses on modality-weighted compute-equivalent tokens. None of them addresses the distinct unit mismatch between decoder placeholder span (`mm_position.length`, used by the scheduler to define chunk boundaries) and encoder embedding count (`get_num_embeds()`, used for compute/cache capacity). This proposal changes only the disabled-chunking validation unit while preserving raw embed-token budget sizing, so it is orthogonal to both cache-reuse policies and modality compute weighting.

findings.title: Efficiently Serving Large Multimodal Models Using EPD Disaggregation
findings.technique_summary: Encode-Prefill-Decode disaggregation separates multimodal encoding from prefill and decode, adds multimedia-token caching, and parallelizes encoding within a request. The target module could adapt its encoder scheduling and cache admission to reduce media TTFT by avoiding encoder-prefill interference and by making repeated media cheap to serve.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "We introduce Encode-Prefill-Decode (EPD) Disaggregation, a novel framework that separates the encoding, prefill, and decode stages onto dedicated resources." Pointer: Abstract, lines 1-2.

findings.title: Continuum: Efficient and Robust Multi-Turn LLM Agent Scheduling with KV Cache Time-to-Live
findings.technique_summary: CacheTTL selectively pins KV cache for tool-call turns using a time-to-live derived from reload/recompute cost and queueing impact. For multi-turn agentic workloads, this could preserve hot conversation state across short tool pauses, reducing repeated prefill TTFT without permanently occupying GPU memory.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "For requests that generate tool calls, CacheTTL selectively pins the KV cache in GPU memory with a time-to-live value determined by the reload cost and potential queueing delay induced by eviction." Pointer: Abstract, line 3.

findings.title: KVFlow: Efficient Prefix Caching for Accelerating LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows
findings.technique_summary: KVFlow replaces plain LRU prefix-cache eviction with workflow-aware eviction and overlapped CPU-to-GPU prefetch based on an Agent Step Graph. The module could use future agent-step metadata, when available, to protect and prefetch likely-next prefixes, improving agentic TTFT and reducing cache-miss stalls.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "KVFlow abstracts the agent execution schedule as an Agent Step Graph and assigns each agent a steps-to-execution value that estimates its temporal proximity to future activation." Pointer: Abstract, line 2.

findings.title: Efficiently Programming Large Language Models using SGLang
findings.technique_summary: RadixAttention stores reusable KV state in a radix tree and uses cache-aware scheduling by matched-prefix length. The module could adapt this idea by ranking waiting requests by resident-prefix benefit, increasing prefix-hit rates for multi-call agent and chat workloads instead of relying only on arrival or static priority.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "we propose RadixAttention, a novel technique that maintains a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache of the Key-Value (KV) cache for all requests in a radix tree". Pointer: Abstract, line 3; cache-aware scheduling is described in Algorithm 1.

findings.title: LLM Query Scheduling with Prefix Reuse and Latency Constraints
findings.technique_summary: The k-LPM scheduler balances longest-prefix-match reuse with fairness under TTFT/TPOT constraints. This gives the module a concrete way to avoid the extremes of FCFS and pure cache-hit prioritization when optimizing median latency for prefix-heavy traffic.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "we present a formal theoretical framework for LLM query scheduling under RadixAttention" and propose "$k$-LPM, which generalizes existing methods by balancing prefix reuse and fairness". Pointer: Abstract, lines 2-3.

findings.title: Optimal Scheduling Algorithms for LLM Inference: Theory and Practice
findings.technique_summary: SLAI uses real-time decode deadline measurements and prompt-length-aware prefill reordering. The module could incorporate deadline/laxity and prompt length into token-budget allocation to lower median TTFT while protecting TPOT.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "SLAI uses real-time measurements to prioritize decode requests that are close to missing their TBT deadlines and reorders prefill requests based on known prompt lengths". Pointer: Abstract, line 3.

findings.title: Taming Throughput-Latency Tradeoff in LLM Inference with Sarathi-Serve
findings.technique_summary: Sarathi-Serve splits long prefills into near-equal chunks and builds stall-free schedules that add prefills without pausing decodes. The module could make chunk sizing and prefill/decode interleaving more adaptive to reduce median TPOT without letting long media or tool prompts dominate a scheduling step.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "Sarathi-Serve introduces chunked-prefills which splits a prefill request into near equal sized chunks and creates stall-free schedules that adds new requests in a batch without pausing ongoing decodes." Pointer: Abstract, line 3.

findings.title: Introducing New KV Cache Reuse Optimizations in NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM
findings.technique_summary: TensorRT-LLM adds priority-based KV eviction with retention priority and duration per token range. The module could extend LRU block eviction with priority/TTL hints for system prompts, agent role prompts, media-derived prefixes, and active sessions that are likely to be reused.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "Priority-based eviction is a new feature of the TensorRT-LLM Executor API that enables users to influence how blocks are selected for eviction." Pointer: section "Priority-based KV cache eviction", lines 4-5.

findings.title: AttentionStore: Cost-effective Attention Reuse across Multi-turn Conversations in Large Language Model Serving
findings.technique_summary: AttentionStore keeps KV caches in a hierarchy of GPU/host/storage tiers and uses scheduler-aware fetch/eviction plus asynchronous layer-wise preload/save. The module could use scheduler hints to decide which remote or lower-tier KV blocks to fetch early and which local blocks to demote, reducing multi-turn TTFT.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "AttentionStore employs layer-wise pre-loading and asynchronous saving schemes to overlap the KV cache access with the GPU computation." Pointer: Abstract, line 4.

findings.title: CacheGen: Fast Context Loading for Language Model Applications via KV Cache Streaming
findings.technique_summary: CacheGen compresses KV tensors into compact bitstreams and adapts compression versus recomputation based on bandwidth. For remote KV loading paths, the module could schedule compressed transfer or recomputation per block to minimize context-loading TTFT under variable network conditions.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "When available bandwidth drops, CacheGen may raise the compression level for a part of the context or choose to recompute its KV cache on the fly." Pointer: publication summary, line 3.

findings.title: Mooncake: A KVCache-centric Disaggregated Architecture for LLM Serving
findings.technique_summary: Mooncake treats KV cache as the central scheduling resource across prefill/decode clusters and CPU/DRAM/SSD cache tiers, with SLO-aware scheduling and prediction-based early rejection. The module could adapt this by making admission and eviction decisions aware of remote-cache residency, transfer cost, and TTFT/TPOT risk rather than only local free-block count.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "The core of Mooncake is its KVCache-centric scheduler, which balances maximizing overall effective throughput while meeting latency-related Service Level Objectives (SLOs)." Pointer: Abstract, line 1.

findings.title: DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving
findings.technique_summary: DistServe co-optimizes prefill and decode placement, resource allocation, and parallelism under separate TTFT and TPOT constraints. The module could use its local scheduling and KV-transfer decisions to better isolate prefill-heavy media or long-context work from decode-heavy traffic.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "DistServe assigns prefill and decoding computation to different GPUs, hence eliminating prefill-decoding interferences." Pointer: Abstract, line 2.

findings.title: VLCache: Computing 2% Vision Tokens and Reusing 98% for Vision-Language Inference
findings.technique_summary: VLCache reuses both encoder cache and KV cache for recurring multimodal inputs, then recomputes only a small, layer-aware subset of vision tokens to control reuse error. This could guide media-cache reuse policies beyond exact prefix hits, reducing media TTFT for repeated images or visual context across agent turns.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "VLCache achieves an accuracy on par with full recomputation, while requiring only 2-5% of the tokens to compute, yielding 1.2x-16x TTFT speedups." Pointer: Abstract, line 2.

findings.title: Embedding Cache
findings.technique_summary: NVIDIA Dynamo uses a CPU-side LRU cache of vision encoder outputs owned by the prefill worker; on hit, it skips the encode worker entirely, and on miss it transfers embeddings via NIXL and stores them. The module could adapt this as a host-tier encoder cache policy for repeated media, reducing GPU encoder load and media TTFT.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "On a hit, the encode worker is skipped entirely. On a miss, the encode worker produces the embedding, transfers it via NIXL, and the prefill worker saves it to the cache." Pointer: How It Works, lines 3-4.

findings.title: ChunkAttention: Efficient Self-Attention with Prefix-Aware KV Cache and Two-Phase Partition
findings.technique_summary: ChunkAttention chunks KV tensors into an auxiliary prefix tree and uses a two-phase partition algorithm to improve locality when many requests share system prompts. The module could schedule prefix-similar requests together and expose richer common-prefix information to downstream attention execution to improve TPOT for shared-prefix batches.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "This is achieved by breaking monolithic key/value tensors into smaller chunks and structuring them into the auxiliary prefix tree." Pointer: Abstract, line 4.

findings.title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion
findings.technique_summary: CacheBlend reuses precomputed KV caches for text chunks even when they are not prompt prefixes, selectively recomputing a small token subset to recover quality. The module could generalize cache lookup and admission beyond strict leading-prefix reuse for repeated tool/RAG context chunks, lowering TTFT in agentic retrieval-heavy workloads.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "We present CacheBlend, a scheme that reuses the pre-computed KV caches, regardless prefix or not, and selectively recomputes the KV values of a small subset of tokens". Pointer: Microsoft Research publication summary.

findings.title: Stateful Large Language Model Serving with Pensieve
findings.technique_summary: Pensieve keeps conversation state across requests using GPU/CPU multi-tier caching and supports attention over non-contiguous cached state. The module could treat multi-turn sessions as stateful cache owners rather than fully freeing all finished-turn state, reducing repeated history prefill for chat and agent loops.
findings.supporting_evidence: Quote: "Pensieve maintains the conversation state across requests by caching previously processed history to avoid duplicate processing." Pointer: Abstract, line 2.
